message.content: {"criteria":[{"id":"C1","level":"Accomplished","mark":8,"evidence":[{"where":"Introduction","quote":"Coral reefs harbour some of the most diverse species of life on the planet"},{"where":"Introduction","quote":"The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education."}],"reasoning":"Primary mission, single satellite rationale, and users (operator and customers) are addressed with context and referenced background. Operator is vague (funding by university or government) and the 'Earth observation' mission is well described. Strong overall but users section is loosely specified and some claims lack citation (e.g. 'Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic' supported by a link).","max":10},{"id":"C2","level":"Adequate","mark":5,"evidence":[{"where":"Launch","quote":"The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle"},{"where":"Orbit","quote":"an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of $ 97.7924^{\\circ} $"},{"where":"Ground Control & Communications","quote":"a Tasmanian facility is selected – the Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory)"}],"reasoning":"Covers all listed elements but with errors: Vega E is unbuilt and launch site rationale contradicts (Kourou at 5.05N, claims two windows incorrectly), RAAN of 27.33° is unjustified, and the orbit semi-major axis and inclination are stated without the J2 derivation. Manoeuvre discussion is thin. Ground-station pass counts are given but contact duration analysis and EOL are weakly supported. Mission duration is 5 years but EOL reasoning includes garbled text. Evidence partly supported by STK screenshots.","max":10},{"id":"C3","level":"Adequate","mark":5,"evidence":[{"where":"Conclusion","quote":"A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet."}],"reasoning":"Conclusion summarises the design and acknowledges the launch risk, but restates content rather than drawing detailed conclusions from the evidence (e.g. average contact times, pass counts, EOL implications). Generic in places.","max":6},{"id":"C4","level":"Adequate","mark":4,"evidence":[{"where":"Executive Summary","quote":"The satellite, nicknamed ZYZZsat (Z-axis/Y-axis Zeroed Zoning Satellite)"},{"where":"Bibliography","quote":"[6] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_in_spaceflight. [Online]."}],"reasoning":"Clear headings and figure set, but many grammar/typo issues, a broken drag sail sentence, unlabelled/unnumbered figures and tables, a Wikipedia source explicitly disallowed, inconsistent citation style, and a contents page mismatch. Presentation falls in the adequate band.","max":6}],"requirements":[{"id":"R1","met":"yes","where":"Introduction"},{"id":"R2","met":"partial","where":"Mission Design"},{"id":"R3","met":"yes","where":"Executive Summary"},{"id":"R4","met":"yes","where":"Introduction"},{"id":"R5","met":"partial","where":"Introduction"},{"id":"R6","met":"partial","where":"Launch"},{"id":"R7","met":"partial","where":"Orbit"},{"id":"R8","met":"partial","where":"Orbit"},{"id":"R9","met":"partial","where":"Ground Control & Communications"},{"id":"R10","met":"partial","where":"Mission Duration & EOL"},{"id":"R11","met":"yes","where":"Ground Control & Communications"},{"id":"R12","met":"partial","where":"Orbit"},{"id":"R13","met":"partial","where":"Contents"},{"id":"R14","met":"no","where":null},{"id":"R15","met":"partial","where":"Bibliography"}],"technical_issues":[{"where":"Launch","issue":"Kourou latitude 5.05°N is described as causing two launch windows per day; the rationale is confused and the claim that equatorial launches need less fuel via 'maximum rotational velocity' is loosely stated."},{"where":"Orbit","issue":"Stated that RAAN must change 360° per year; the sun-synchronous precession is about 0.9856°/day (~360°/year) but the text calls it a 1° daily east precession and the RAAN value 27.33° is unjustified."},{"where":"Orbit","issue":"Table lists semi-major axis 6971km and Argument of Latitude 0° as a fixed value, yet u changes with time; no epoch or orbital period given."},{"where":"Mission Duration & EOL","issue":"Uncontrolled re-entry at 600 km is described as burning up; at 600 km it may take decades, so the disposal claim is not supported by a lifetime calculation."},{"where":"Mission Duration & EOL","issue":"Text 'to ' and drag sail sentence are truncated; the drag sail discussion is incomplete."},{"where":"Ground Control & Communications","issue":"Access table shows duplicated row 14 and 15 and an unnumbered row '----'; average contact claim of ~10 min matches 580 s but 15 passes listed inconsistently with the 'first fifteen' label."}],"overall":"The report covers most required segments with STK support but has significant technical inconsistencies, unbuilt launch vehicle selection, weak justification of orbit and EOL, incomplete drag sail discussion, unlabelled figures and a disallowed Wikipedia source. Presentation and conclusion are adequate rather than strong."}
